plain.text: As people multiplied on the earth, the "sons of God" took wives from the daughters of men. (Readers have long discussed who these "sons of God" were.) The LORD said his Spirit would not contend with humans forever; their days would be 120 years. There were giants, called Nephilim, on the earth in those days. The LORD saw how great the wickedness of mankind had become, and that every inclination of their hearts was only evil all the time. The LORD regretted that he had made man, and his heart was deeply troubled. He said he would wipe out what he had made.

But Noah found favour in the eyes of the LORD. Noah was a righteous man, blameless in his generation, and he walked faithfully with God. He had three sons. The earth was corrupt and full of violence in God's sight.

God told Noah he was going to put an end to all people, because the earth was filled with violence. He told Noah to build an ark of cypress wood, coated with pitch, and gave its measurements: about 450 feet long, 75 feet wide and 45 feet high, with a roof, a door and three decks. God would bring floodwaters on the earth. "But I will establish my covenant with you." Noah, his wife, his sons and their wives would enter the ark, along with two of every kind of living creature, male and female, to keep them alive, and food for them all. Noah did everything just as God commanded him.

summary.bigIdea: The world is full of violence and God is grieved, but Noah walks with God and is told to build an ark.
points: Human wickedness grows until God's heart is deeply troubled.
Noah finds favour with God and walks faithfully with him.
God promises a covenant with Noah, and Noah does all that God commands.
summary.reflection: God's heart was "deeply troubled" by violence. What does that tell you about how God feels about the wrong in the world?
